claim: C1: Board card menu stays open with a live full-page backdrop after keyboard focus tabs out (src/components/CardMenu.tsx:99-198)
evidence: Opened menu via keyboard (focus + Enter) on /board. Tabbed 5x through the 4 menu items and out to document.body (activeElement=BODY, outside both .zui-cardmenu-pop and .zui-cardmenu). At that point .zui-cardmenu-pop and .zui-cardmenu-backdrop were both still in the DOM and visible (popVisibleAfterTab=true, backdropExistsAfterTab=1), aria-expanded on the trigger stayed 'true', and continued Tab presses moved normally through the rest of the page chrome (top-icon, top-brand, search input) proving it is NOT a keyboard focus trap - only a visual/pointer-interception leak. document.elementFromPoint(20,20) returned the .zui-cardmenu-backdrop div (position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:40, no background so fully invisible), proving it intercepts pointer events across the whole viewport. Decisive proof: with the stale menu/backdrop still open, a real mouse click was fired directly on a SECOND, unrelated card's '...' menu button elsewhere on the board; the click was swallowed by the backdrop instead of opening that button's menu (popCountAfter=0, secondBtnExpanded=false) - a legitimate control's click was silently eaten. The backdrop's own onClick does call close(), so Escape (verified: closes, popCountAfterEsc=0) and any single outside click (verified: closes, popCountAfterOutsideClick=0) both recover it - it is not a permanent lock, but the first click after tabbing away is silently lost with zero visual feedback.

claim: C2: Every route overflows horizontally at 320px + 200% zoom, from fixed-width top-bar icons (src/App.css:31-45,62-70 - .top, .top-icon)
evidence: Tested at 320px viewport with document.documentElement.style.zoom='2' applied AFTER goto (verified this actually changes layout: body.clientWidth halves to 160 while window.innerWidth/documentElement.clientWidth stay 320, matching real page-zoom semantics; avoided the addInitScript trap). All 9 routes (/, /board, /board/9001, /feed, /insights, /companies, /people, /cv, /settings) showed identical document.documentElement.scrollWidth=446 vs clientWidth=320 -> 126px horizontal overflow on every single route. After filtering out elements shielded by a nearer overflow-x:hidden/auto/scroll ancestor (the naive widest-element search falsely flagged internally-scrolled board columns and a today-ascent strip), the actual unclipped, document-overflow-causing element on all 9 routes was .top-corner.end (containing .top-icon, the fixed 38px settings icon button) with rect.right=446.36 - matching scrollWidth (446) almost to the pixel. /cv additionally showed .cv-rail-step also breaching at 390 width but that never exceeded the top-icon's contribution.

claim: C3: Board search focus indicator reuses the gold that already failed the project's own 3:1 contrast bar (src/App.css:5172-5175)
evidence: `.board-bar:focus-within { border-color: var(--accent); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--accent-soft); }` uses --accent = #d6a441 (src/index.css:96) as the focus indicator border. Computed WCAG relative-luminance contrast (verified formula reproduces the codebase's own documented numbers to 2 decimals): #d6a441 vs --surface #ffffff (the input pill's own background) = 2.27:1; vs --bg #f4f2ec (the page ground the pill sits on) = 2.03:1. Both fail SC 1.4.11's 3:1 minimum. This is not a new finding - src/index.css:343-348 has an existing comment on the generic `:focus-visible` rule stating verbatim 'The gold ring measured 2.27:1 against a white card and 2.03:1 against the paper ground... under-contrasted', which is why that rule was already changed to use --accent-ink (#836427, clears 4.5:1) instead of --accent. .board-bar:focus-within at App.css:5172-5175 was missed in that fix and still points at the failing --accent.

claim: C4: Stage-change and CV-variant-delete buttons under 24px target size (src/App.css:929-940,5866-5876 .detail-rail-step; src/cv/cv.css:166-197 .cv-rail-del)
evidence: Mixed result across the two selectors, measured live at /board/9001 and /cv at 1280px and (both fine-pointer-emulated and real touch-emulated) 390px. .detail-rail-step: at 1280px and at 390px WITHOUT touch emulation (pointer:fine, e.g. a resized desktop window) measured 88.3x20.1px / 81x20.1px - height fails the 24px minimum. Checked the spacing exception: same-column adjacent steps sit 21.7px apart center-to-center, which is LESS than the 24px needed for their notional 24px-diameter target circles to avoid overlapping, so the exception does not save it - a genuine SC 2.5.8 failure for mouse/fine-pointer users. However, re-tested with a real touch emulation (hasTouch:true, isMobile:true, matchMedia('(pointer:coarse)') confirmed true) and the existing `@media (pointer: coarse) { .detail-rail-step { min-height: 44px } }` rule (App.css ~5866-5876) actually engages, measuring 44px height on every step - compliant on real phones, which is the product's declared first-class surface. .cv-rail-del: measured 13.375x21px at both viewports and both pointer types (its own pointer:coarse fix only adds an invisible ::after hit-overlay, confirmed present at 44x44px under touch, but the visible box itself never grows). Checked spacing: nearest other target (the adjacent .cv-rail-step) measured 75.7px away center-to-center in the seeded data, and the rail's own flex layout (row height ~40px + 0.15rem gap) keeps repeated .cv-rail-del instances ~40px+ apart vertically in any multi-variant case - comfortably clearing the 24px spacing-exception threshold on both pointer types. So: .detail-rail-step is a real, confirmed target-size failure but only for mouse/fine-pointer users at any viewport (not for the touch/mobile audience the product prioritizes, which already gets a 44px fix); .cv-rail-del is undersized but the spacing exception genuinely applies and it is not a violation.

claim: C5: Board card company chip hard-clips mid-word; the ellipsis rule is inert (src/App.css:5548 - .bstrip > span)
evidence: `.bstrip > span { display: flex; ...; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap }` (App.css ~5548-5556). The missing property is not overflow/width/white-space (all present) - it is that the element is `display: flex` rather than block/inline-block: per the CSS Overflow spec, text-overflow only renders on block containers, and is a documented no-op on flex containers. Confirmed live at /board (1280px): of 12 `.bco` company/contact spans measured, 8 had scrollWidth > clientWidth (genuinely clipped, e.g. 'Brightpath Talent Partners · Sanne Verhoeven' clipped by 195px, 'Ferro & Vale Recruiting · Ingrid Sorel' by 145px), and in every clipped case textContent contained no '…' or '...' - a hard mid-word clip with zero ellipsis rendered, exactly as claimed. The board.tsx source (src/board.tsx line ~115) even has a comment acknowledging this: 'this cell clips hard: measured 56px of box against 288px of content' - and works around it with a hover `title` tooltip rather than fixing the ellipsis.
